title: WD J0558-1449 stays about 45 % dimmed with grey colour to March 2026 in ZTF difference images and had excess Gaia DR3 scatter in 2014-2017, unlike six one-off dimming white dwarfs
abstract: Question: Is the new deep dimming of the white dwarf (WD) WD J0558-1449 (Gaia DR3 2992629136205665152, G = 19.86), found in ZTF DR24 catalogue light curves by campaign study sci:842147d0, real in a method that does not use the catalogue? What are its depth, onset and colour, does it continue after 2025-10, and was the WD variable before? Approach: We did PSF forced photometry on 993 ZTF difference images (2018-09 to 2026-03-30, two fields, IRSA cutouts, including 5 months after DR24) and reference-free aperture photometry on the science images. We ranked the Gaia DR3 G-band scatter proxy A_G against same-G white-dwarf-like Gaia sources, for this WD and for 24 other dimming or debris-transit WDs. Results: Both methods show the event. It starts at MJD 60626 +/- 12 (2024-11) with a 47-day e-folding time. The WD is at 0.58 of its 2018-2024 flux in g and r after 2025-02, while 17 comparison stars stay at 0.96-1.03, and it is still at 0.53-0.63 in 2026-01/03 with no recovery trend. The colour exponent ln f_g / ln f_r is 0.85 (95 %: 0.68-1.08); interstellar-type dust (1.38) is excluded at 5.4 sigma, so the occulter is grains larger than about 1 um or opaque clumps. In Gaia DR3 (2014.6-2017.4) the WD has A_G 2.4 times the median of same-G WDs (2 of 2,084 as high; 1 of 769 colour-matched); in ZTF the 2018 season is 8 % low and the season-to-season scatter exceeds that of all comparison stars. None of the six one-off events of van Roestel et al. (2026) has excess Gaia scatter (p 0.17-0.92; this WD p = 0.009), while 7 of 8 known debris-transit WDs have 1.6-3.8 times the median. A ring screen at the tidal radius needs at least 4e16-4e17 g of dust. We also confirm a shallow 2023 dimming of WD J2010+0259 (13 % in g, 8 % in r, 4-7 times the comparison-star spread). Limitations: Only ZTF and Gaia data exist; there is no spectrum, no second telescope in the event and no high-cadence light curve. The Gaia proxy cannot separate a few deviant transits from continuous variability, and ZZ Ceti pulsation is not fully excluded. The dust mass rests on an assumed geometry. The J2010+0259 test removes a proper-motion dipole trend with a neighbouring-season comparison.

display.caption: WD J0558-1449 relative flux from forced PSF photometry on ZTF difference images (top: 2018-2026; bottom: the event). Blue: g; red: r; circles field 306, squares field 1349. Diamonds: season means with empirical errors. Lines: logistic fit (onset MJD 60626, tau 47 d, depth 0.45 g / 0.47 r). Crosses (bottom): reference-free aperture photometry relative to 11 comparison stars. The dashed line marks the end of ZTF DR24 used by sci:842147d0. Grey band (top): Gaia DR3 photometry window, in which the WD had 2.4 times the median G-band scatter of same-G WDs.

Left: rank of the Gaia DR3 G-band scatter proxy A_G = sqrt(n_obs)/(flux/error) of each WD among same-G white-dwarf-like Gaia sources in the same HEALPix pixel, as -log10 p. WD J0558-1449 (red) has p = 0.009; the six one-off events of van Roestel et al. (2026) are normal; many known debris-transit WDs and the Gaia-selected B25 candidates are high. Right: A_G of 2,084 same-G WD-like sources (light) and 769 with BP-RP 0-0.25 (dark); the red line is WD J0558-1449.

Depth in g against depth in r for 24 nights with both bands in the 2025-2026 part of the WD J0558-1449 event. Dashed: grey (equal depth). Orange: interstellar-type dust (A_g/A_r = 1.38). Red: fitted depth ratio 0.88. The colour exponent ln f_g/ln f_r = 0.85 (95 %: 0.68-1.08) excludes interstellar-type dust at 5.4 sigma.

citations.reason: Discovery of the WD J0558-1449 event and of the weak WD J2010+0259 case in ZTF DR24 catalogue light curves; source of the Gaia IDs of comparison WDs. We confirm both with independent forced photometry and extend WD J0558-1449 to 2026-03.
van Roestel et al. 2026: one-off deep obscuration events of WDs; we use their coordinates for the Gaia scatter comparison and compare the activity history.
Bhattacharjee et al. 2025: debris-transit candidates, used as a Gaia-selected reference group.
Gentile Fusillo et al. 2021 Gaia EDR3 WD catalogue: T_eff and mass of WD J0558-1449.
Gaia DR3 summary paper (Gaia Collaboration, Vallenari et al. 2023).
Bellm et al. 2019: the Zwicky Transient Facility.
Masci et al. 2019: ZTF science data system, difference images and PSF products.
Related campaign search of TESS data of nearby WDs for transits.
